title: App Entry & Bootstrap
description: The application bootstraps from src/main.ts, which mounts the root Svelte component and injects Vercel analytics. App.svelte is the monolithic root component that wires together every UI section—equipment slots, enchantment panels, weapon art selectors, and damage output displays. This step gives you the big picture before diving into the engine.

title: Type System & Game Data
description: types.ts defines the core domain types—StatMap, BuildState, Enchantment, WeaponBlade/Handle, MonkGlove/Essence, and the stat-key taxonomy. Every downstream module depends on these contracts. Understanding StatKey, StatMap, and the upgrade system (applyUpgrade) is essential before reading the engine.

title: State Management (The Store)
description: store.ts is the single source of truth. It creates a Svelte writable store for BuildState, persists it to localStorage with debounced saves, and derives the computed result via calcBuild(). All UI mutations flow through exported helpers (setEnchantment, setGuild, moveArmorSlot). The derived 'result' store is what powers every damage display in the app.

title: JSON Game Data & Lookup Functions
description: The engine/data/ directory loads and indexes all game items from JSON files in src/data/—armors, blades, handles, gloves, essences, rings, runes, enchantments, races, and guilds. It exposes getter functions (getBlade, getArmorPart, getEnchant, etc.) used throughout the engine. This is the bridge between raw game data and the calculation pipeline.

title: Weapon Calculation
description: weapon.ts resolves the weapon type from blade+handle combinations (Dagger, 2-Handed Sword, Dual Wielding, etc.), applies shrine multipliers, and computes stat scalings. It also handles monk glove/essence calculation with rank-based multipliers. The weapon result feeds into every damage formula downstream.

title: Enchantment System
description: enchant.ts applies enchantment stat modifiers to equipment slots using a two-phase approach: first applying selector-based transforms (positive/negative stats, defenses), then direct stat and perk modifiers. It handles exclusive vs. stacked enchantments, upgrade scaling, and returns the final stats and perk values for a slot.

title: Core Damage Calculation Engine
description: build.ts is the heart of the application. calcBuild() takes the full BuildState and computes final stats, perk values, cooldown reduction, damage type bonuses, boost multipliers, crit values, and per-attack damage (M1, M2, WA). It orchestrates enchantment application, shrine effects, buff/boost assembly, racial bonuses, and guild rank effects into a single result object.

title: Constants, Buffs & Perk Definitions
description: The constants/ directory contains every hardcoded game value—damage type colors and priorities, crit formula thresholds, CDR data, buff definitions, boost multipliers, defensive calculations, and draconic system constants. The parallel src/data/ directory holds calculation modules for buffs (BuffData.ts), race effects, potions, weapon arts, and summon data that feed into the build engine.

title: UI Components & Shared Primitives
description: The UI layer includes domain-specific components (DamageAnalyzer, BaseDamageCalc, BuffList, BuildSaves, WeaponStatsDisplay) and shared primitives in src/lib/ui/ (Badge, Button, RollValue). Modal dialogs for equipment selection live in src/lib/modals/. These components read from the derived 'result' store and render the computed damage breakdown, stat summaries, and interactive build controls.

title: Build Tools, Saves & Polish
description: BuildSaves.ts handles saving/loading named builds to localStorage. Supporting components like CdrStepsCalc, EmotionalTracker, PropellingFunTracker, and LevelBar expose interactive controls for toggling game-specific mechanics. DidYouMean and tag/stat filter components provide search UX for the equipment modals. This step covers the finishing touches that make the app production-ready.
